FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
A steady circular red still allows a permitted turn on red after yielding, whereas a steady red arrow means remaining stopped for that direction as long as the arrow stays red [A01].
Why it matters: group red-signals; difficulty high; prereq sec08-F07; confusables sec08-F07, sec08-F09 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
A left turn on a circular green must yield to oncoming vehicles, while a left-turn green arrow usually means the opposing traffic is stopped [A01].
Why it matters: group green-signals; difficulty high; prereq sec08-F04; confusables sec08-F04, sec08-F05 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A02
A circular flashing yellow means proceed with caution, but a circular flashing red is treated exactly like a stop sign with a complete stop and yielding [A02].
Why it matters: group flashers; difficulty medium; prereq sec08-F11; confusables sec08-F10, sec08-F11 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A02
A yellow X over a lane warns that the lane is about to close or reverse so you should leave it soon, while a red X means the lane is already closed or carrying opposing traffic and must not be used [A02].
Why it matters: group lane-signals; difficulty medium; prereq sec08-F13; confusables sec08-F13 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A03
A broken yellow line on your side permits passing when safe, but a solid yellow line on your side forbids passing entirely [A03].
Why it matters: group yellow-lines; difficulty high; prereq sec08-F19; confusables sec08-F19, sec08-F20 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A03
A broken white line between same-direction lanes allows a lane change without straddling, whereas a solid white line between same-direction lanes means do not change lanes [A03].
Why it matters: group white-lines; difficulty high; prereq sec08-F21; confusables sec08-F21, sec08-F22 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A03
A reversible lane bordered on both sides by double broken yellow lines is the only place a driver may travel left of a yellow line, while a center left-turn lane with solid yellow outside and broken yellow inside is for left turns only [A03].
Why it matters: group special-lanes; difficulty high; prereq sec08-F24; confusables sec08-F24, sec08-F25 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A01
Turning right on red is allowed at an intersection of two-way streets, but turning left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, both after yielding and absent a prohibiting sign [A01].
Why it matters: group turn-on-red; difficulty high; prereq sec08-F08; confusables sec08-F08, sec08-F07 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A02
The hand symbol or don't walk indication forbids pedestrians to cross while the walking figure or walk indication permits it, yet a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane has the right-of-way everywhere regardless of a crosswalk [A02].
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty medium; prereq sec08-F15; confusables sec08-F15, sec08-F17 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A01
The round or diamond yellow sign is the advance warning of a railroad crossing, while the white X crossbuck marks the crossing itself and a sign beneath it counts the tracks when there are two or more [A01].
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty medium; prereq sec08-F01; confusables sec08-F01, sec08-F02 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A03
Wide white stop lines mark exactly where to stop at an intersection, whereas solid white crosswalk lines run fully across the pavement and mark a space a car must never block [A03].
Why it matters: group intersection-lines; difficulty medium; prereq sec08-F27; confusables sec08-F26, sec08-F27 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0051]
